prompt: Two angles of a triangle measure $40^\circ$ and $75^\circ$. What is the third angle, in degrees?
hint: The three angles of ANY triangle always add to $180^\circ$.

hints.text: The three angles of ANY triangle always add to $180^\circ$.
First add what you know: $40 + 75 = 115$. Then see what is missing from $180$.

explanation: The two known angles add to $40 + 75 = 115$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Tear the corners off
steps: Cut a paper triangle and tear off all three corners.
Slide the three torn corners together and they form a perfectly straight line — and a straight line is 180°.
So the missing corner is whatever is left over: 180 − 115 = 65°.

alternativeExplanations.title: Work backwards
steps: Start at the full 180° and take away the pieces you already have.
Same answer, one subtraction at a time — handy when the numbers are messy.
